The study, published in the International Journal of Electronic Marketing and Retailing, considered papers from the four leading specialist journals in this area.

more.title: Baby lobster decline foreshadows major midcoast population losses, study shows
more.summary: A steep drop in baby lobsters provided an early warning of the sharp decline in adult lobsters along Maine's midcoast, a new University of Maine study shows.

more.title: Ramp reaches $60B valuation as it pushes deeper into AI
more.author: Ram Iyer
more.summary: The funding comes as Ramp's annualized revenue crosses $2B, and its customer count reaches 85,000.

more.title: Targeting the cell cycle for cancer therapy: From the discovery of CDK9 to precision medicine and beyond
more.summary: More than 30 years after the direct connection was established between the molecular machinery controlling cell division and cancer, a new paper traces the evolution of cyclin-dependent kinase research and outlines the next generation of CDK-targeted therapies.

more.title: Tech giants want clean energy in N.C. Is Duke finally ready to help?
more.author: Elizabeth Ouzts
more.summary: In North Carolina, tech giants and other large corporations that want their own 24/7 carbon-free electricity have a problem. Across most of the state, only Duke Energy, the state’s vertically integrated utility, can sell them power, and the company’s grid isn’t required to be 100% clean until mid-century. For the…

more.title: AI turns scrap impurities into useful ingredients for stronger recycled iron
more.summary: About 2 billion metric tons of metal are produced worldwide every year to meet the demands of industry, infrastructure and the energy sector. Much of this production still relies on primary raw materials, contributing to an estimated 40% of industrial greenhouse gas emissions and 10% of global energy consumption.

more.title: NASA Welcomes All Ages, Experience Levels for Space Apps Challenge
more.summary: Registration is open for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, a two-day global event on Saturday, Nov. 14 and Sunday, Nov. 15, where teams work to create solutions inspired by NASA’s most ambitious exploration goals and making use of the agency’s free and open data. The annual challenge, often called a hackathon, is an intensive, […]

more.title: Exclusive: Chariot Raises $10M To Help Consumers Fight Back Against Hidden Fees And Hard-To-Cancel Subscriptions
more.author: Judy Rider
more.summary: New York-based Chariot Claims has raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Silverton Partners to help consumers pursue claims over alleged privacy violations, hidden fees and subscriptions that are difficult to cancel.

more.title: First in-depth map of 'forever chemicals' in the Finger Lakes created
more.summary: In 2023, professor Damian Helbling was getting a lot of calls and emails from local residents. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) had just announced regulations to limit per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—some of which have been linked to cancers and other negative health effects—in drinking water.

more.title: How Do Fungi Keep the Planet Healthy?
more.author: Steven Strogatz and Janna Levin
more.summary: Evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers explains how fungal networks in soil trade nutrients with plants, help keep carbon underground, and strike bargains without having a brain. The post How Do Fungi Keep the Planet Healthy? first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: Endangered species in Canada face extensive delays receiving protection
more.summary: For more than 20 years, Canada's Species at Risk Act (SARA) has protected wildlife that are at risk of being lost from Canadian lands and waters. Once a species is listed as extirpated, endangered or threatened under the act, it becomes illegal to kill, harm or capture it or damage its residences. Its critical habitat must also be protected, at least on federal land.

more.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
more.summary: Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park.

more.title: Neutron's first launch slips again amid trouble with carbon composites
more.author: Stephen Clark
more.summary: Rocket Lab announced the Neutron rocket in 2021, aiming for a first flight in 2024.

more.title: Mysterious brain activity under anesthesia challenges what we know about consciousness
more.summary: Even under general anesthesia, the human brain can analyze language, recognize different types of words, and predict what comes next in a story, according to a surprising discovery by Baylor researchers. The findings challenge our understanding of consciousness and suggest that the unconscious brain is far more capable than scientists previously realized.

more.title: A fungus is threatening the world’s food supply. Scientists just found a new defense
more.summary: Scientists have discovered a potential new weapon against a devastating fungus that threatens rice, wheat, and barley worldwide. By engineering a special type of plant immune receptor, researchers created defenses capable of recognizing multiple fungal threats at once.

more.title: Scientists discover a surprising danger in smaller cancer cells
more.summary: Scientists have discovered that unusually small cancer cells carrying extra chromosomes can be far more aggressive than larger ones, growing faster, spreading more readily, and resisting common treatments. The surprising finding could help explain why some tumors are especially dangerous and provide a new way to predict cancer outcomes.

more.title: In animated films, nonhuman characters are still overwhelmingly male
more.summary: Female protagonists in animated films have come a long way over the past several decades. Take the 1959 movie "Sleeping Beauty": Soft-spoken and vulnerable, Princess Aurora is cursed as an infant by the evil fairy Maleficent and ultimately saved not by her own wits, but by a prince's kiss.

more.title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
more.author: Lucas Ropek
more.summary: The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March.

more.title: And the winner of Startup Battlefield at Disrupt 2026 is: Intero Biosystems
more.author: Sean O'Kane
more.summary: Intero Biosystems beat out 199 other Startup Battlefield companies to take home the $100,000 grand prize at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.

more.title: Rare study reveals a striking divide inside an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain
more.summary: A rare examination of an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain revealed that regions cleared of amyloid plaques had remarkably little of the harmful tau buildup associated with memory loss, while neighboring areas showed extensive damage. The discovery suggests that removing amyloid may have lasting protective effects and could help slow Alzheimer’s progression, especially when treatment begins early.

more.title: Imperial woodpecker returns to life as a detailed digital specimen
more.summary: Researchers have created a detailed, animated 3D model of the imperial woodpecker (Campephilus imperialis), a spectacular bird that has not been confirmed in the wild since 1956. The model, built from a museum specimen and the only known film footage of the living bird, is freely available to scientists, educators and the public.

more.title: White Sands footprints suggest humans experienced abrupt environmental shifts during the last ice age
more.summary: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park in New Mexico have provided researchers an opportunity to refine the age of the oldest human footprints in North America and establish a deeper understanding of the landscape and environmental conditions at the time humans were present there.
